patients.summary: Software engineer in Amherst with HIV/AIDS on intermittently taken Biktarvy, followed at an outside HIV clinic, who joins in 2021. Over five years he develops ulcerative colitis, neurocysticercosis, 40% TBSA burns, miliary TB, cryptococcal meningitis, PML, and CMV esophagitis and colitis, mostly known to the practice through brief outside documents.

conditions.label: Human immunodeficiency virus disease
conditions.note: AIDS, CDC stage 3; followed at outside HIV clinic

medications.drug: bictegravir 50 MG / emtricitabine 200 MG / tenofovir alafenamide 25 MG Oral Tablet
medications.reason: HIV infection; prescribed by outside HIV clinic

procedures.procedure: Office visit, new patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
34M here to establish primary care. Moved his care here from a group practice; does not have those records and isn't sure they'd tell us much.

HIV: diagnosed before he came to us; followed at an outside HIV/ID clinic, which prescribes Biktarvy one tablet daily. He was told his counts put him in the AIDS range, CDC stage 3. Doesn't know his most recent CD4 or viral load. Candid that he misses doses, sometimes several days in a row, mostly when work gets busy. No prior opportunistic infections that he knows of. He has the clinic's number and plans to keep them as his HIV doctors; wants us for everything else.

Other meds: multivitamin daily. NKDA.
PMH otherwise none. No surgeries.
FHx: father with high blood pressure, mother with type 2 diabetes, an uncle on his father's side with ulcerative colitis. Nobody with immune problems or neurologic disease that he knows of.
Social: software engineer, mostly remote. Lives in Amherst with his partner. Never smoked, no alcohol, no drugs.
Vaccines: COVID primary series this spring (pharmacy). Doesn't recall a tetanus shot or any pneumonia or meningitis vaccine.

ROS: negative in detail. Appetite fine, weight stable, bowels normal.

Exam: well, thin build. Vitals per flowsheet. HEENT clear, no thrush. No lymphadenopathy. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no organomegaly. Skin without rash. Neuro nonfocal.

A/P
1. HIV infection with AIDS (stage 3), on Biktarvy via HIV clinic, adherence intermittent. Talked about why daily dosing matters with this regimen; he'd like a phone reminder approach. Will request HIV clinic notes and labs.
2. Health maintenance: Tdap, PCV20 and MenACWY #1 today (all indicated with HIV). MenACWY #2 in 8 weeks. CBC, CMP, lipids, A1c (family hx), HCV Ab.
3. PHQ-9 3.
Return in about 6 months or sooner as needed.

documents.title: Vaccines Administered
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Tdap 0.5 mL IM L deltoid. PCV20 0.5 mL IM R deltoid. MenACWY 0.5 mL IM R deltoid, 1 inch below prior site. VIS given for each. Tolerated, observed 15 minutes without reaction.

documents.title: Your new-patient labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Raul, your blood count, kidney and liver tests, cholesterol and A1c all came back normal. Hepatitis C test negative. Nice meeting you last week. See you in the winter, sooner if anything comes up.

documents.title: Records Request
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Faxed signed release to outside HIV clinic for recent notes and labs. Called to confirm receipt; told the request is in their queue.

documents.title: Nurse Visit — Vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Here for second MenACWY. Feels well, no fever. 0.5 mL IM L deltoid. Tolerated. Series complete. Still nothing back from HIV clinic re: records; re-sent request.

documents.title: Nurse Visit — Vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu shot L deltoid and COVID booster (Pfizer) R deltoid. Eligible for booster given immunocompromise. No reaction during observation.

documents.title: stomach issue
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I've had loose stools on and off since around the end of the summer and it's gotten worse. Now there's some blood in it. Going 6 or more times a day and waking up to go. Should I come in?

documents.title: RE: stomach issue
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Yes, we'd like to see you. Booked you Tuesday 1/11 at 2:00. If you get high fevers, dizziness, or a lot of blood, go to the ED.

results.text: No Salmonella, Shigella, Campylobacter or Shiga toxin-producing E. coli isolated

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Loose stools since roughly late August, gradually worse. For the past couple of months 6-8 a day with blood and mucus, gets up 1-2x at night. Tired. Appetite down; scale at home says he's lost weight. No vomiting. Denies travel, antibiotics, anyone sick at home. Thinks he's been taking Biktarvy "most days."

O: Vitals per flowsheet. Weight 69 kg, was 73 in July. Looks tired, mildly pale. Abdomen soft, mild tenderness low on both sides, no guarding. No masses.

A/P: ~4.5 months of bloody diarrhea with weight loss in a man with AIDS. Infection first: stool culture and O&P (kit given, drop off tomorrow), CBC, CMP, ESR. With his uncle's UC, IBD is on the list. Referring to GI now rather than waiting on results. Call if fever or worse bleeding.

documents.title: Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Raul — stool culture and parasite test are negative. Your blood count shows mild anemia, and the inflammation marker (ESR) is up, which fits an inflammatory process in the colon. I've sent all of this to GI. Their office should call you to schedule; let us know if you haven't heard by the end of next week.

documents.title: Gastroenterology Consultation
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Date of visit: 02/28/2022
Reason for referral: hematochezia and chronic diarrhea

Thank you for sending Mr. Ramos, 35, who has HIV with AIDS. For about six months his stools have been loose and increasingly frequent, now six to eight a day with visible blood and mucus, and some nights he wakes to go. He estimates an unintended loss of 5 kg (11 lb) over the last three months, with occasional low-grade fevers, fatigue and less appetite. No recent travel or antibiotics, no ill contacts, no camping or untreated water.

On review of systems he mentions stiff, aching knees and ankles in the mornings that loosen up as the day goes on, and red, mildly sore eyes for a few weeks. No rash, oral ulcers or chronic back pain.

Medications: he tells me he takes a daily multivitamin. Biktarvy is prescribed by his HIV clinic; he acknowledges taking it intermittently. NKDA.
Family history: paternal uncle with ulcerative colitis who had some kind of intestinal surgery in his 40s; he doesn't know the details. Father with hypertension, mother with type 2 diabetes.
Social: software engineer; no tobacco or alcohol.

Exam: T 37.9 C, BP 118/74, HR 84, RR 14. Mildly pale, comfortable. Abdomen soft with mild tenderness in both lower quadrants, no rebound or guarding, no hepatosplenomegaly or mass, bowel sounds normal. Rectal: gross blood mixed with stool. Perianal exam without fistula or abscess.

Data: your January labs show a mild normocytic anemia and an elevated ESR; stool culture and O&P negative.

Impression: presentation most consistent with ulcerative colitis. Infectious colitis, including CMV given his immune status, must be excluded on biopsy.
Plan: colonoscopy with biopsies, scheduled for 3/22. Will start therapy once histology is back. We will keep you informed.

Allergies: NKDA

Gastroenterology

medications.drug: mesalamine 1200 MG Delayed Release Oral Tablet
medications.sig: Take 4 tablets (4.8 g) by mouth once daily with food

reports.text:
Specimens: A. rectum, B. sigmoid colon, C. descending colon, D. transverse colon, E. ascending colon, F. terminal ileum (cold forceps biopsies).
A-C: Colonic mucosa with chronic active colitis, crypt architectural distortion, basal lymphoplasmacytosis and cryptitis with focal crypt abscesses. No granulomas. No viral cytopathic effect; CMV immunostain negative. No dysplasia.
D-E: Colonic mucosa without diagnostic abnormality.
F: Small bowel mucosa without diagnostic abnormality.
reports.conclusion: Chronic active colitis involving rectum through descending colon, consistent with ulcerative colitis. Negative for CMV, granulomas and dysplasia.

documents.title: Colonoscopy Report
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Procedure date: 03/22/2022. Indication: hematochezia, chronic diarrhea, suspected IBD.
Sedation: monitored anesthesia care. Prep adequate. Cecum and terminal ileum intubated; withdrawal 11 minutes.
Findings: From the anal verge continuously to the mid-descending colon, erythematous mucosa with loss of vascular pattern, friability and scattered shallow ulcerations. Sharp transition to normal mucosa in the proximal descending colon. Transverse colon, ascending colon, cecum and terminal ileum normal. Segmental biopsies taken.
Pathology: chronic active colitis rectum through descending colon, CMV stain negative, no granulomas or dysplasia; proximal colon and ileum normal.
Impression: left-sided ulcerative colitis.
Plan: mesalamine DR 4.8 g once daily (prescription sent). GI clinic follow-up in about 3 months. Repeat CBC/creatinine with PCP.
Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Pharmacy — Prior Authorization
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy called: mesalamine DR 1.2 g needed PA through the insurer. GI's office already submitted it; approved 4/1 per the plan. Patient picked up first fill. Nothing for us to do; FYI to PCP.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
UC f/u. Colonoscopy in March showed left-sided UC, biopsies negative for CMV. On mesalamine 4 tabs daily since late March, says he hasn't missed it — "it's easier when you can feel the difference." Now 1-2 formed BMs/day, no blood, no nighttime stools. Energy better. Knee and ankle stiffness gone. Eyes fine.
Biktarvy: "better than before."
Weight 69.5, up a bit. Abd soft, NT.
A/P: UC in remission on mesalamine. CBC and creatinine today (mesalamine monitoring). Keep GI f/u. HIV per ID clinic — encouraged him to get his labs there; still no records from them.

documents.title: Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good news: anemia has resolved and kidney function is normal on the mesalamine. No changes.

reports.study: MRI brain without and with contrast
reports.text: Multiplanar multisequence MRI of the brain before and after gadolinium. Multiple enhancing lesions at the gray-white (corticomedullary) junction bilaterally. Ventricles and sulci normal for age. No hydrocephalus. No midline shift. Major flow voids preserved.
reports.conclusion: Multiple enhancing lesions at the corticomedullary junction.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Date of service: 08/27/2022
CC: headache, fever, confusion

35M with HIV/AIDS and ulcerative colitis brought in by partner. Three weeks of headaches getting steadily worse, low-grade fevers, diffuse muscle aches, and over the last days increasing confusion. Back about a month from a humanitarian trip to rural Guatemala.
Meds: Biktarvy (intermittent), multivitamin, mesalamine. NKDA.

Exam: T 38.3. Oriented to self only. Mild weakness of the right arm and leg. Fundi without papilledema. Neck supple.

Toxoplasma IgM and IgG: negative.
MRI brain w/wo contrast: multiple enhancing lesions at the corticomedullary junction.

MDM: multiple enhancing brain lesions in an AIDS patient with recent travel to an endemic area. Neurosurgery consulted; biopsy deferred pending further workup. Admitted to medicine with ID consult.

Disposition: admitted.
Allergies: NKDA

documents.title: Raul is in the hospital
documents.author: patient
documents.body: This is Raul's partner writing from his account. He was admitted Saturday night with fever and he was really confused. They found spots on his brain MRI and think it may be from the trip to Guatemala. They're doing more tests. Just wanted you to know.

documents.title: RE: Raul is in the hospital
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thank you for letting me know — I'm sorry. Please have him or the team call us when he's discharged so we can see him within the week. We'll ask the hospital to send records.

conditions.label: Neurocysticercosis
conditions.note: admitted 8/27-9/2; treated with albendazole and dexamethasone

medications.sig: Take 2 tablets (400 mg) by mouth twice daily with food for 14 days
Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily during albendazole, then taper as directed

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen with partner after admission 8/27-9/2 at the regional hospital. We have the ED record only; no discharge summary yet. History from patient, partner and the pharmacy fill list.

They tell me: brain MRI showed multiple lesions; toxo blood tests were negative; a blood test for the pork tapeworm came back positive and the team called it neurocysticercosis, presumably picked up in Guatemala. No biopsy. He was started on albendazole twice a day for 14 days plus dexamethasone, and the confusion cleared over the first few days. No seizures. Discharged home 9/2.
Fill history matches: albendazole 200 mg #56 and dexamethasone 4 mg, both filled 8/30.

Now: headaches much less, no fever. Partner says he's "back to himself." Taking albendazole with meals; 4 days left, then the steroid taper.

Exam: alert, oriented x3, conversational and appropriate. Speech normal. CN intact. Strength 5/5 in all four limbs, no drift. Gait normal. Lungs clear, heart regular.

A/P
1. Neurocysticercosis, on treatment, neuro exam normal today. Finish albendazole; follow steroid taper as written. Seizure precautions reviewed; no driving restrictions given since no seizures, but call or go to ED with any episode. Requesting discharge summary.
2. HIV/AIDS — asked him to see the HIV clinic soon; he has an appointment later this month.
3. UC — quiet on mesalamine.
Flu and COVID shots next month.

documents.title: Records Request
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Faxed request to regional hospital HIM for discharge summary and labs from admission 8/27-9/2.

documents.title: Nurse Visit — Vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Influenza L deltoid, bivalent COVID booster R deltoid. Feels well. Finished his steroid taper last month. No reaction.

documents.title: Refill — mesalamine
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy refill request for mesalamine DR 1.2 g, take 4 daily. GI prescription out of refills; patient says GI follow-up is in January. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: RE: Refill — mesalamine
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Approved 90 days, 1 refill, to bridge to his GI visit.

documents.title: Records Follow-up
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Second request to regional hospital for 8/27 admission discharge summary. HIM says it was "sent"; nothing in our fax log. Re-faxed request.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam, 36M.

Interval: neurocysticercosis admission Aug/Sept, treated with albendazole + dexamethasone; no headaches or seizures since. Hospital discharge summary still never arrived despite two requests. UC: 1-2 formed stools/day, no blood on mesalamine 4.8 g; saw GI last week, no changes. HIV: on Biktarvy via ID clinic; says adherence is "70, 80 percent." We talked about pill-box plus phone alarm again.

Meds: Biktarvy daily, mesalamine DR 1.2 g x4 daily, multivitamin. NKDA.
Social: working, partner well. No tobacco or alcohol.
ROS negative.

Exam: well-appearing. Vitals per flowsheet, weight 72 (back to baseline). HEENT normal, no thrush, no nodes. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Skin intact. Neuro: alert and oriented, strength and gait normal.

A/P
- HIV/AIDS: per ID clinic; adherence counseling.
- UC in remission on mesalamine; CMP for creatinine.
- Neurocysticercosis, treated, asymptomatic.
- Prevention: Shingrix #1 today (recommended at any adult age with HIV); #2 in 2-6 months. Lipids, A1c (mother with T2DM), CBC. PHQ-9 2.
RTC 6 months.

documents.title: Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Raul, all of your labs from Tuesday look good — blood count, kidneys, liver, cholesterol and A1c are normal. Book Shingrix #2 any time from March on.

events.reason: burns from house fire, inhalation injury

conditions.label: Sepsis due to burn wound infection

documents.title: Burn Center Discharge Summary
documents.author: surgery
documents.body:
Regional burn center
Admitted: 03/02/2023  Discharged: 04/21/2023

Diagnoses: second- and third-degree thermal burns, 40% TBSA, sustained in a house fire; inhalation injury; burn wound infection with sepsis (resolved); sinus tachycardia secondary to burns. Background: HIV/AIDS, ulcerative colitis.

Course: Arrived intubated for inhalation injury and was mechanically ventilated in the burn ICU. On arrival BP 95/60, HR 120, T 38.2 C; abdomen soft and non-distended. Hemodynamically stable with formula-guided fluid resuscitation. Persistent sinus tachycardia attributed to the burn injury. Underwent staged excision and split-thickness skin grafting. Tracheostomy placed for prolonged ventilation; weaned and decannulated before discharge. Course complicated by burn wound infection with sepsis, treated with IV antibiotics, resolved. Home ART resumed once taking enterally. Mesalamine resumed.

Discharge condition: stable, ambulating, grafts healing.
Discharge meds: home medications (Biktarvy, mesalamine, multivitamin).
Follow-up: burn clinic in 1 week; outpatient PT/OT; PCP in 1 week; HIV clinic.
Allergies: NKDA

documents.title: Call from Partner
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Partner called. There was a fire at their home early Thursday morning (3/2). Raul has serious burns and smoke inhalation, intubated in the burn ICU at the regional burn center. Partner was not badly hurt. Asked that we be aware; no requests right now. Offered support; gave practice number for anything they need. PCP informed.

documents.title: RE: Call from Partner
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called partner back to check in. Will plan to see him within a week of discharge. Sent a note to the burn center team with his med list and that he's followed by an outside HIV clinic.

conditions.label: Personal history of thermal burns, 40% total body surface area
Sepsis due to burn wound infection

documents.title: Post-Discharge Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
First visit since the house fire. Burn center stay 3/2-4/21; we don't have the discharge summary yet, history from Raul and partner.

They describe: intubated for smoke inhalation, burns on about 40% of his body, several trips to the OR for excision and skin grafts, a tracheostomy that was taken out before he left, and a serious wound infection with sepsis partway through that needed IV antibiotics. Home 4/21. Seeing burn clinic weekly, PT/OT twice a week.

Now: sore and tight at the graft sites, sleeping poorly. Eating better. No fever. Biktarvy: honest that he missed a lot since getting home — "there's been a lot going on." Mesalamine every day; stools formed, no blood.

Exam: thin, tired, moving carefully. Vitals per flowsheet; weight 64 kg, down 8 from January. Healed tracheostomy site. Graft sites dressed by burn clinic, not taken down. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Abdomen soft.

A/P
1. Major burns s/p grafting, burn wound sepsis resolved. Burn clinic and therapy managing wounds. Nutrition: protein at every meal, multivitamin.
2. HIV/AIDS with missed doses. Hasn't been to the HIV clinic since discharge. Drawing CD4 today and sending it to them; asked him to book there this month.
3. Weight loss after the admission — follow.
4. Hgb mildly low after a long stay; CBC today, recheck in 2 months.
RTC 2 months.

documents.title: Your blood tests
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Raul, your CD4 count is 180, which is low and means the HIV isn't controlled well right now. It's the daily Biktarvy that brings it back up. I faxed the result to your HIV clinic. Blood count is a little low after the hospital stay and kidney and liver tests are fine. Please let me know once you have the HIV clinic appointment.

documents.title: RE: Your blood tests
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Got it. Appointment is the 18th. I'll try to do better with it.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
2 months after burn center discharge. Grafts closed per burn clinic, now every 4-6 weeks. Still in OT for hand/shoulder range of motion. Sleeping better.
Saw HIV clinic in May; says they "restarted the conversation" about adherence. Admits still missing some days.
UC quiet.
Discharge summary from the burn center did arrive in early May; reviewed, matches what they told me.

Wt 66 (up 2). Grafted skin intact, no open areas where visible. Lungs clear. Heart regular.

A/P: recovering well. Shingrix #2 today — series complete. CBC to recheck Hgb. Next physical January; flu/COVID in the fall.

documents.title: Blood count
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Blood count is back to normal. Nothing to do.

documents.title: Missed Appointment

documents.body: No-show for 2:30 follow-up. Left voicemail to reschedule.

documents.title: Nurse Visit — Vaccines
documents.author: RN

documents.title: Discharge Summary — Infectious Diseases
documents.author: infectious diseases
documents.body:
Admitted 10/30/2023, discharged 11/09/2023.
Principal diagnosis: miliary tuberculosis. Other: HIV/AIDS with nonadherence to ART; anemia.

36M with HIV/AIDS (CD4 180 in April) who has taken ART irregularly, admitted with three weeks of fevers, drenching night sweats and a dry cough, and 5 kg weight loss over the past month. T 38.9 C, HR 110, diffuse crackles on auscultation. Hgb 10.2, WBC 4.5, plt 250. Na 135, K 4.2, Cr 1.1. ALT 45, AST 50, alk phos 120. HIV RNA 120,000 copies/mL; CD4 50. CXR with innumerable 1-2 mm nodules through both lung fields. TST 0 mm at 48 h (anergic in this setting).

Airborne isolation. Sputum NAAT positive for M. tuberculosis complex, rifampin resistance not detected; culture grew M. tuberculosis, susceptible to isoniazid, rifampin, pyrazinamide and ethambutol. Started RIPE with pyridoxine 11/01. Because of rifampin, Biktarvy was stopped and ART changed to dolutegravir 50 mg BID plus emtricitabine/tenofovir DF daily; return to Biktarvy 2 weeks after rifampin ends.

Discharge meds: rifampin 600 mg daily, isoniazid 300 mg daily, pyrazinamide 1500 mg daily, ethambutol 1200 mg daily, pyridoxine 50 mg daily (all DOT via local health department); dolutegravir 50 mg BID; emtricitabine/tenofovir DF 200/300 mg daily; mesalamine DR 4.8 g daily; multivitamin.
Follow-up: health department TB clinic; HIV clinic 2 weeks; PCP 1 week with CBC and LFTs.
Allergies: NKDA

documents.title: Post-Discharge Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hospital f/u, admitted 10/30-11/9 for miliary TB. Discharge summary received 11/14 and reviewed.

Feeling better. Fevers and sweats gone, cough much less. Health department nurse watches him take the TB pills on weekday video calls. No nausea, no RUQ pain, no tingling, vision unchanged. Taking the new HIV regimen (dolutegravir twice daily + Truvada) — says having the TB nurse check in has helped him with those too.

Exam: thin, no distress. Vitals per flowsheet; weight 60. Lungs: a few scattered crackles, much better than described. Heart regular. Abdomen soft, no hepatomegaly. No jaundice.

A/P
1. Miliary TB on RIPE + pyridoxine via health dept DOT. LFTs today (ALT/AST mildly up on admission) and at each visit while on PZA. Reviewed hepatitis warning symptoms.
2. HIV/AIDS, CD4 50, VL 120k on admission. ART changed for rifampin interaction. HIV clinic appt 11/22.
3. Anemia, Hgb 10.2 on admission — adding to list. CBC today; likely inflammation from the infection, follow.
4. UC quiet on mesalamine.
RTC 6-8 weeks.

documents.title: Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Liver tests are normal on the TB medicines — good. Hemoglobin about 10, where it was in the hospital. We'll keep checking both.

documents.title: Call from Health Department
documents.author: RN
documents.body: TB program nurse from the local health department called to coordinate. Patient on daily DOT by video, good attendance so far. Asked that we keep checking LFTs; next due at his January visit. Fax number for results given.

medications.reason: intensive phase completed 1/2 per health department
intensive phase completed 1/2 per health department

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TB f/u. Health dept letter: 2-month intensive phase completed 1/2; pyrazinamide and ethambutol stopped. Continues rifampin + isoniazid + B6 through about the end of April, still DOT.
Feels "almost normal." No fever or sweats since November, cough gone. Eating well, weight 63 (up almost 3). No numbness or tingling, vision fine, no abdominal pain.
HIV: on dolutegravir BID + Truvada. Saw ID clinic in December — no numbers in hand.
UC: formed stools, no blood.

Exam: looks better. Vitals per flowsheet. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Abdomen soft, no liver edge. Skin: no jaundice; graft sites well healed.

A/P
1. Miliary TB, continuation phase. LFTs today.
2. Anemia improving — CBC.
3. HIV/AIDS per ID; back to Biktarvy two weeks after rifampin ends, per their plan.
RTC 3-4 months; physical in the summer.

documents.title: Results
documents.author: PCP

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Date of service: 04/25/2024
CC: headache x 2 weeks, fever, stiff neck

37M, HIV/AIDS, recent miliary TB (on rifampin/isoniazid), UC. Two weeks of headache that keeps getting worse, fevers, and neck stiffness. Acetaminophen hasn't touched it. CD4 50 at his HIV clinic a month ago.
Meds: dolutegravir BID, emtricitabine/tenofovir DF, rifampin, isoniazid, pyridoxine, mesalamine. NKDA.

Exam: T 38.9. Uncomfortable. Resists neck flexion, painful. Fundi: no papilledema. Nonfocal otherwise.

LP: opening pressure 250 mm H2O. CSF WBC 20/mm3, 90% lymphocytes; protein 100 mg/dL; glucose 20 mg/dL (serum 90). India ink: encapsulated yeast seen. Culture sent.

Impression: cryptococcal meningitis.
Plan: ID consulted, induction antifungal therapy to start in ED; admit to medicine.
Allergies: NKDA

documents.title: Back in the hospital
documents.author: patient
documents.body: It's Raul's partner again. He's in the hospital since yesterday with meningitis, they said it's a fungus (cryptococcus). He'll be there about two weeks for IV treatment. He's more comfortable today.

documents.title: RE: Back in the hospital
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thank you for telling us. Please call when he's going home so we can see him that week.

documents.title: Post-Discharge Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Admitted 4/25-5/9 for cryptococcal meningitis. ED record received 4/30; no discharge summary yet. History from Raul, partner and his bottles/fill list.

Per them: spinal fluid culture grew Cryptococcus; two weeks of IV liposomal amphotericin plus flucytosine pills; finished his last TB doses in the hospital on 5/1 (health dept confirmed by phone). Sent home on fluconazole 800 mg daily (4 x 200 mg) for 8 weeks, then a lower dose. HIV clinic switched him back to Biktarvy yesterday — dolutegravir and Truvada stopped.

Now: headache gone. No fever. Tired. No vision change. Eating OK.

Exam: thin. Vitals per flowsheet; weight 59. Alert, oriented, fluent. Neck supple. CN intact, strength and gait normal. Lungs clear. Heart regular.

A/P
1. Cryptococcal meningitis, consolidation fluconazole 800 mg. CMP/Mg after amphotericin.
2. Miliary TB — treatment complete 5/1. Resolved; personal history of TB on the list.
3. HIV/AIDS — back on Biktarvy daily. Talked again, plainly, about how these infections tie to missed doses. He gets it; asked for help setting up pharmacy blister packs — sent request.
4. Anemia — CBC.
5. Med list reconciled: Biktarvy, fluconazole 800, mesalamine 4.8 g, multivitamin.
RTC July for physical.

documents.title: Call from Partner
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Partner called with Raul on speaker. About two weeks of a weak left arm — dropping things — and trouble walking, "like he's drunk but he isn't." Mild headache. No fever, no stiff neck, no light sensitivity. Partner adds he's been forgetful and "not himself" in his personality.
Given AIDS and prior CNS infections, needs imaging and neurology now. Spoke with neurology on call: urgent clinic slot Friday 10/18 with MRI the same morning. Advised ED immediately for any fever, neck stiffness, seizure, sudden worsening or new trouble speaking or swallowing. Partner will drive. They agree.

reports.study: MRI brain without and with contrast
reports.text: Multiplanar multisequence MRI of the brain before and after gadolinium. Multiple T2/FLAIR hyperintense white matter lesions that do not enhance. No mass effect or surrounding edema. No hydrocephalus. No acute infarct on diffusion imaging. No abnormal meningeal enhancement.
reports.conclusion: Multiple nonenhancing white matter lesions without mass effect or edema.

documents.title: Neurology Consultation
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Date of visit: 10/18/2024

Thank you for the urgent referral of Mr. Ramos, 37, with poorly controlled HIV/AIDS and cryptococcal meningitis earlier this year. Two weeks of progressive weakness of the left arm and difficulty walking, with a mild headache. No fever, neck stiffness or photophobia. His partner describes increasing forgetfulness and a change in personality. He says his ART has been irregular because of social circumstances.

Meds: Biktarvy, fluconazole 200 mg daily, mesalamine, multivitamin. NKDA.

Exam: alert, attentive enough for the exam. Left hemiparesis. Gait ataxic. No meningismus.

Data: CD4 150 today; viral load elevated per HIV clinic. MRI brain (this morning): multiple nonenhancing white matter lesions without mass effect or edema.

Impression: progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy in the setting of uncontrolled HIV.
Plan: lumbar puncture for CSF JC virus PCR. There is no specific antiviral treatment; immune recovery on consistent ART is the treatment, coordinated with his HIV clinic. Outpatient physical therapy. Neurology follow-up in 3 months.

Addendum 10/28/2024: LP performed 10/22. CSF JC virus PCR positive, confirming PML.

Neurology

medications.reason: dose increased for presumed Candida esophagitis

medications.sig: Take 2 tablets (400 mg) by mouth daily for 14 days, then resume 1 tablet daily

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
About a week of pain when he swallows, food feeling like it sticks, and a burning ache behind the breastbone with eating. Eating less; down 3 kg since January. No vomiting, no blood. No mouth sores or blisters that he's noticed. On fluconazole 200 daily, says he's been taking it.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet; weight 60. White plaques on tongue and buccal mucosa that scrape off — thrush. No vesicles or ulcers in the mouth. Neck: no nodes. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Abdomen soft, nontender.

A/P: odynophagia/dysphagia with oral thrush in advanced HIV — presume Candida esophagitis. Raise fluconazole to 400 mg daily (2 of his 200 mg tabs) x 14 days, then back to 200. If no better within a week, he needs endoscopy — CMV and HSV are the other possibilities. Call sooner for fever, inability to keep fluids down. Messaged HIV clinic.

documents.title: Follow-up Call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called to check in at one week. No better — swallowing still very painful, mostly liquids now, chest pain with every swallow, low-grade temps at home. Failed a week of higher-dose fluconazole. Needs admission for endoscopy and IV support. Called the regional hospital GI service, who will take him; told him to come in through the ED tonight or first thing in the morning. Partner will bring him.

reports.text:
Specimen: esophagus, mid and distal ulcer biopsies.
Squamous mucosa with ulceration and granulation tissue. Enlarged endothelial and stromal cells with intranuclear inclusions; CMV immunohistochemistry positive. PAS/GMS negative for fungal organisms. HSV immunostain negative. No dysplasia.
reports.conclusion: Ulcerative esophagitis with cytomegalovirus inclusions (CMV IHC positive). Negative for fungi and HSV.

documents.title: Discharge Summary — Gastroenterology
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Admitted 04/17/2025, discharged 04/24/2025.
Diagnosis: cytomegalovirus esophagitis. Other: HIV/AIDS with irregular ART, oral thrush, ulcerative colitis, PML, prior cryptococcal meningitis on maintenance fluconazole.

38M with two weeks of odynophagia, dysphagia and retrosternal pain with 5 kg weight loss and low-grade fevers, no better after a week of fluconazole 400 mg for presumed candidiasis. No oropharyngeal vesicles. ART taking has been irregular, he says because of social circumstances. Oral thrush on exam. CD4 50.

EGD 4/18: several well-circumscribed ulcers in the mid and distal esophagus; no plaques. Biopsies: CMV inclusions confirmed by IHC; no fungal organisms, HSV negative.
Treated with IV ganciclovir, transitioned to oral valganciclovir once swallowing improved.

Discharge meds: valganciclovir 900 mg BID through 5/8 (21 days total); fluconazole back to 200 mg daily; Biktarvy daily; mesalamine DR 4.8 g daily; multivitamin.
Follow-up: PCP 1 week with CBC (valganciclovir); HIV clinic.
Allergies: NKDA

medications.sig: Take 2 tablets (900 mg) by mouth twice daily with food through 5/8

Swallowing much better — soft solids without pain. No fever. On valganciclovir 900 BID with food through 5/8. Fluconazole back to 200 daily. Biktarvy daily, says the hospital stay "scared him straight" again.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet; weight 58. Mouth: no thrush now. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Abdomen soft. Neuro: left-sided weakness and gait as before.

A/P
1. CMV esophagitis on valganciclovir — CBC today for counts; BMP for creatinine (dosing).
2. Thrush cleared — resolved.
3. HIV/AIDS, CD4 50 in hospital — HIV clinic 5/7.
4. Weight 58 — small frequent meals, add shakes.
RTC July.

documents.body:
Admitted 10/24/2025, discharged 10/31/2025.
Diagnosis: cytomegalovirus colitis. Other: HIV/AIDS with nonadherence to ART; ulcerative colitis; prior CMV esophagitis (April 2025); PML; prior cryptococcal meningitis on fluconazole; anemia.

38M admitted with two weeks of crampy lower abdominal pain and frequent small-volume bloody stools. T 38.2 C, BP 100/60, HR 110. Cachectic, weight 55 kg. Diffuse abdominal tenderness without rebound or guarding. Hgb 10.2, WBC 4.5, plt 150. CD4 40; HIV RNA 120,000 copies/mL.

Colonoscopy 10/25: multiple ulcerations in the sigmoid colon, biopsied. Pathology: CMV inclusions on IHC with background chronic colitis consistent with his UC.
IV ganciclovir, then oral valganciclovir. Mesalamine continued. Bleeding settled by discharge.

Discharge meds: valganciclovir 900 mg BID through 11/14 (21 days total); Biktarvy; fluconazole 200 mg daily; mesalamine DR 4.8 g daily; multivitamin.
Follow-up: PCP within 1 week, CBC; HIV clinic; GI clinic.
Allergies: NKDA

Admitted 10/24-10/31, CMV colitis on sigmoid biopsies (background UC). Summary received 11/4, reviewed.

Cramping much less. Stools 3-4/day, no blood for the last few days. No fever. Valganciclovir 900 BID through 11/14, mesalamine, fluconazole, Biktarvy.
CD4 40 and viral load 120k in hospital — second CMV infection in six months. We had a long, direct talk about ART: he wants to do this; what gets in the way is the bad weeks, when everything slides. Partner sets out the blister pack with his coffee now. HIV clinic 11/12.

Exam: very thin. Vitals per flowsheet; weight 55. No thrush. Abdomen soft, mildly tender lower, no guarding. Neuro as before.

3. UC — mesalamine continues.

Annual exam, 39M.

No hospital stays since October. Says this is the longest stretch he's felt steady in a few years. Working full days again from home.
HIV: Biktarvy daily from blister packs; HIV clinic every 3 months. Fluconazole 200 daily continues per them.
UC: 1-2 stools, no blood. Mesalamine.
PML: left hand still clumsy for fine tasks, gait unsteady but he's doing the home exercises. Memory unchanged per partner.
Mood good; PHQ-9 3.

Meds: Biktarvy daily, fluconazole 200 mg daily, mesalamine DR 4.8 g daily, multivitamin. NKDA.
Social: lives with partner. Never smoker, no alcohol.

Exam: thin, well-appearing. Vitals per flowsheet; weight 58. HEENT: no thrush, no oral lesions. No lymphadenopathy. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Skin: healed graft sites. Neuro: left arm and leg weaker than right; wide-based gait.

A/P
- HIV/AIDS on Biktarvy, cryptococcal maintenance fluconazole — per HIV clinic.
- UC in remission — CMP.
- PML with stable residual deficits.
- Anemia — CBC.
- Prevention: lipids, A1c. Vaccines current; flu/COVID this fall. Colorectal screening not yet due by age; GI will plan UC surveillance.
Follow-up in September.
